entry.title: Jane Street and Rivals Are Now Fighting for AI Power as Well as Pace (17 minute read)
entry.content:
High-frequency traders are now racing for compute. They are investing in the sector as it secures them access to greater processing capacity and faster chips. These firms primarily profit from tiny price differences as they move rapidly in and out of positions. As they increasingly rely on machine learning, their success is directly tied to their computing power. While the risks are significant, most high-speed traders see few options if they want to avoid becoming obsolete.

entry.title: Neural chip decodes interactions between brain regions (7 minute read)
entry.content:
Researchers have developed an implantable neural chip that tracks communication across brain regions. It can record brain activity and extract biomarkers that describe the strength of brain waves and synchrony between signals from different brain regions. These signals can be decoded using a machine-learning algorithm to distinguish between cognitive and emotional states. The capability to extract brain-network biomarkers to trigger precisely timed stimulation has many applications across next-generation neurotechnology.

entry.title: US military gives Elon Musk's SpaceX access to sensitive tracking data (7 minute read)
entry.content:
SpaceX has been granted access to restricted space tracking data by the US military. The access raises new national security questions as well as questions about whether the Trump administration is attempting to hand over traffic control in Earth's orbit to a donor. Elon Musk's Doge program fired many of the federal government's space traffic control staff in 2025, and the administration has twice attempted to financially gut the Traffic Coordination System for Space department. The moves have been widely viewed in the industry as an attempt by Musk to privatize space traffic control.

entry.content:

TSMC sends engineers to Arizona on contracts of up to three years, with families moving from Taiwan to the site. This article looks at the impact the factory had on Phoenix, the employees who moved to America to work there, and the chip manufacturing industry in the US.

His work, along with just a handful of others, has allowed countless websites and organizations to fix the recently revealed PHP vulnerabilities quickly. entry.title: Physicists trap and tame single particle of antimatter for months (12 minute read)
entry.content:
Physicists at Northwestern University have coaxed a single positron (the antimatter counterpart of an electron) into an exquisitely controlled quantum state for the first time. The scientists cooled the fast-moving particle to nearly absolute zero after capturing it from radioactive decay, and then suspended it in a near-perfect vacuum, resulting in a state where the positron behaved much like an artificial atom with quantum energy levels scientists can precisely control and observe. The technique could enable the most precise test yet of a fundamental symmetry between electrons and their antimatter counterparts.

entry.title: How Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins (16 minute read)
entry.content:
Anthropic asked an internal research model to design mini binders, small proteins that attach tightly to a target, against scorpion neurotoxins as part of its work in experimenting with how Claude can accelerate drug discovery. 17 of the 211 designs tested met Anthropic's criteria. Anthropic has not confirmed whether these binders neutralize scorpion venom in a cellular environment, so it is not claiming to have produced an antivenom. However, the study is a promising first step towards using AI to design credible binders against hard-to-target toxins in days, with lab confirmation within weeks. The challenge, as always, will be turning those binders into safe, affordable, and widely accessible drugs.

entry.title: How To Use Decision Models for Evals (23 minute read)
entry.content:
Decision models are an appealing alternative to LLM judges for automated evals. However, whether they're the right choice depends on the cost, performance, and latency requirements of the use case. Many people leave the default decision threshold at 0.50 without checking whether that's appropriate for the task, leaving a lot of performance on the table. This post shows how to tune thresholds to get the best results from decision models, compares cost and performance between models, and explores how to interpret model scores and how calibration can make them more useful.

entry.title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models (16 minute read)
entry.content:
Clairic is an extraction model. Extraction models are a new class of System One-style models that can extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs, all at significantly higher accuracy, faster latency, and lower cost than traditional LLMs. It answers with values directly extracted from the input, computed from it, or predicted beyond it. The model can't produce a mistyped answer or hallucinate in the same way an LLM can, but it can still make mistakes.

entry.title: Decoherence (48 minute read)
entry.content:
Decoherence is the accumulation of locally valid but mutually incompatible or redundant models within a system. It causes the cost of change to be dominated by translating among those models and preventing unintended side-effects. Decoherence grows relative to the rate of change of a system, and it increases faster the more decoherent a system is, resulting in runaway exponential growth. It rules out the specter of runaway recursive self-improvement, as decoherence both prevents AI from improving in a bubble and limits the rate at which it can improve outside of it. However, it also introduces a new kind of disaster called Decoherence Collapse.

Meta had delayed the release of Muse for months due to safety concerns. However, the success of an AI agent created by a startup called Instinct led Mark Zuckerberg to push for a launch due to fear of losing a competitive edge. The launch was successful and has given Meta an early lead with agents. The agent has only had a few safety hiccups, like when it gave out a user's address to a seller on Facebook Marketplace without permission.

entry.title: Apple Is About to Close the Biggest Hole In Its Ecosystem With HomeView (17 minute read)
entry.content:
Apple is set to unveil new smart home products tomorrow. The centerpiece will be a smart home hub called the HomeView that essentially serves as the Siri command center for an Apple-powered household. There will be a countertop model with a metal base and a wall-mounted version with a flat, square base that sits against the wall beneath the display. The HomeView will only support a limited selection of Apple applications, and there will be no App Store for downloading additional software.

entry.title: China's Delivery Robots Are Learning to Tackle the Night Shift (11 minute read)
entry.content:
Shenzhen opened access for nighttime deliveries by driverless vehicles in March. Night operations make otherwise idle vehicles and infrastructure productive. It also means quieter roads, reduced pedestrian traffic, and lower congestion. Driverless vehicles eliminate the cost of a human: they don't need night shift wages, they don't get tired, and they don't need to be paid extra for driving in the rain.

entry.title: Problems in 22 scientific fields had solutions hiding in plain sight. An AI has found them (7 minute read)
entry.content:
Borrowing an idea from one research discipline to solve a problem in another is an age-old scientific trick. However, such clever leaps are rare because researchers don't tend to spend their time researching fields outside of their expertise. AI can easily hop between fields. BootLoops is a harness that can spot and solve problems in seemingly unrelated fields that share the same mathematical structures at massive scale. Researchers recently released 36 preprints produced with BootLoops covering a wide range of topics, including figuring out the age of sunspots, analyzing government health policies, and attempting to decipher a mysterious medieval manuscript.

entry.title: So long, Spokes: GitHub rewrites storage to restore reliability, just in time for agentic hordes (5 minute read)
entry.content:
GitHub is rebuilding its Git storage architecture from scratch. Early internal testing shows a promising 35x write improvement. The plan involves decoupling writes from reads, offloading maintenance, and letting object storage manage redundancy. The change won't alter developer workflows, review processes, or security controls.

Venture-capital firms are helping startups obtain computing capacity.
